findings.reason: the section names one mechanism (a kind-scoped supersede order in `review_lifecycle`) whose input the store cannot hold, so the plan must either key the figure record distinctly (kind or review run in the staging filename) or state that the two reviews land at different heads, before a node builds the test its done-when requires.
findings.text: §18's whole premise is that a stored text review and a figure review of the same run coexist in the store and are told apart by `review_kind`, and its done-when requires "a stored text review followed by a figure review reads both as current", but the staging store keys a run's review record by the reviewed run and its head alone — `review_path` returns `<store>/<project>/<reviewed_run_id>.at-<head>.json` (`reckon/crew/review.py:2111`) — and its own reader documents the store as holding "one record per round — at different heads" (`stored_records_for_run`, `reckon/crew/review.py:3576`). A figure review dispatched for the same run at the head the text review read (§6 composes both from the same base→head) writes the same path and replaces the text review's record, so the kind-scoped supersede order this section adds never sees two records and cannot produce the done-when it asserts

findings.reason: the change lives in `review_lifecycle.lifecycle`, which both callers already reach, so narrowing the rationale names the same implementation and alters no node.
findings.text: §18 says "every reader that consults supersession, the routing view and the obligations view among them, would drop the text review's findings", but a run review's supersession is consulted only by the obligations view (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:1097`, `_review_is_hot`); the routing view's two `is_hot` calls (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2583`, `:2589`) pass plan records and never a run id, so routing would not drop a run text review's findings

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py` resolves; the test file is declared new, and `reckon/crew/figure_review.py` is declared new by §6, which §18 depends on.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §18's done-when is measurable and carries a declared negative control ("with `review_kind` left out of the supersede order, the figure review supersedes the text review and the test fails"), which removes exactly the mechanism under test.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §18's gate requires every log written under the run directory with its revision, the literal command and a trailing `EXIT=`, a durable path rather than a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — descriptive module and test names, no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §18 now declares one deliverable (supersession scoped by review kind); the promotion refusal and the repair reflex have moved to §19 and §20, each with its own verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §18 declares `scoring-should-stop-a-promotion#s6` in `plan-section-depends-on` (the section that writes `review_kind`), and §19/§20 depend on §18; every depends-on target resolves to a section that exists.
